title: OpenbookLM
description: A local-first alternative to Google NotebookLM that goes beyond answering questions - It will be your local private agent that reads documentation, understands your codebase, and writes the code to implement it.
details: OpenBookLM solves the privacy and fragmentation issues of modern technical work by providing a local-first workspace that turns sensitive documentation, research papers, and codebases into actionable engineering progress without cloud dependencies. It helps developers and researchers deeply understand complex architectures through syntax-aware retrieval and other offline tools, while bridging the gap between passive reading and real execution by autonomously writing, refactoring, and verifying code directly within their local repositories.

title: A.D.S.A.
description: An open-source autonomous agent that plans, codes, and runs complete data science workflows inside an isolated local sandbox.
details: An open-source autonomous data science system inspired by DeepAnalyze-8B, designed to turn raw tabular data into analytical reports without manual script writing.
highlights: End-to-end execution. Parse datasets, choose an analytical strategy and write code for EDA, cleaning, feature engineering and statistical modeling.
Isolated iteration. Execute generated Python in a sandbox, inspect errors and revise scripts while blocking unsafe system calls.
Readable outputs. Produce narrative technical reports with visualizations and key performance metrics.

title: Polymarket Analyzer
description: Tracking Polymarket events, filtering market news strictly for our specific equity holdings, and generating daily trading reports tied to real stock movements.
details: Built an automated, scheduled data pipeline to evaluate whether prediction markets offer an early trading edge on specific equity holdings:
highlights: Scheduled ingestion. Use GitHub Actions on intervals from 5 minutes to 5 hours to collect Polymarket contracts and scraped news with Beautiful Soup or Selenium.
Focused daily reports. Combine holdings-specific odds with Tavily news and FMP analyst targets, using Groq or Gemini LLMs to produce structured Markdown reports without unrelated market noise.
Verify and cache. Compare resolved contracts with Yahoo Finance price history; store signals, holdings and reports in Supabase junction tables, with a 6-hour cache for deep-dive queries.

title: Autonomous 4WD Rover
description: Implementing real-time perception, spatial scanning, and state-based navigation on resource-constrained embedded hardware.
details: Built a real-time autonomous 4-wheel mobile rover driven by a deterministic perception —> decision —> action pipeline:
highlights: Active scanning. Mount an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor on a micro-servo to scan left and right when an obstacle crosses the distance threshold.
State-based navigation. Use C++ logic to compare available paths and trigger evasive maneuvers through an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver.
Embedded constraints. Manage power distribution, motor back-EMF and hardware interrupts to support stable sensor polling and locomotion.

title: Zombie Shooter AI
description: Trained a tabular reinforcement learning agent to balance evasion, targeting, and survival in a custom 2D arcade environment.
details: Built and trained a discrete reinforcement learning agent from scratch to master a custom-built 2D survival arcade game:
highlights: Model the environment. Translate screen position, nearby zombies and directional alignment into a discrete state space.
Train the policy. Implement Bellman updates and epsilon-greedy exploration across more than 5,000 episodes, rewarding survival and eliminations while penalizing damage.
Inspect the learning. Run headless training or real-time visual sessions; log NumPy .npz metrics and inspect reward curves and policy heatmaps in Jupyter.

title: Gomoku Game AI
description: A competitive board game engine using minimax, threat-space pruning, and pattern heuristics to outplay humans and adversarial agents under strict turn timers.
details: Engineered a competitive AI game agent capable of playing Gomoku (Five-in-a-Row) against both human players and opponent algorithms within a strict 10-second turn limit:
highlights: Search efficiently. Use depth-variable minimax with alpha-beta pruning and iterative deepening, respecting a 10-second cutoff per turn.
Limit the branching. Consider moves near existing stones instead of evaluating every empty space on the board.
Score the threats. Apply positional heuristics to five-in-a-row, open and blocked fours, and other sequences across horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines.
